title: Repeated strategy promotion tests versus a sequential likelihood rule
prompt: All observations, parameters and trading arrangements are synthetic. Each day is an independent Bernoulli success under either of two fully specified hypotheses: H0 success probability 0.5, H1 success probability 0.7. A success is positive after-cost daily P&L; observations contain no magnitude information. Production monitoring promotes the strategy at the first day when the cumulative likelihood of observed outcomes under H1 divided by that under H0 is at least 1/alpha. There is no lower stopping boundary. Monitoring ends after 18 days if no promotion occurs. For comparison, a naive researcher tests each day using the exact one-sided binomial H0 tail P(number of successes >= observed successes), and promotes at the first p-value <= alpha without correcting repeated looks. Return both first promotion days for the supplied path, the production likelihood ratio at stopping, its EXACT probability of promoting by day 18 under H0, and the anytime false-promotion upper bound from the nonnegative likelihood-ratio martingale. Day numbering starts at 1; use 0 for no promotion.

outputs.name: likelihood_at_stop
outputs.description: Ratio when the production boundary is first reached.

outputs.name: naive_fixed_test_stop_day
outputs.description: First uncorrected fixed-sample test promotion day, or 0.

outputs.name: finite_horizon_false_promotion
outputs.description: Exact H0 probability the production boundary is reached by day 18.

outputs.name: anytime_false_promotion_bound
outputs.description: Upper bound valid over arbitrarily many looks.
